title: The Jet That Ran Out of Fuel at 41,000 Feet
alt_titles: One Wrong Number Turned a Jet Into a Glider
Out of Fuel, No Engines, 69 People: The Gimli Glider
description:
On 23 July 1983, Air Canada Flight 143, a brand-new Boeing 767 carrying 69 people, ran out of fuel at 41,000 feet over Canada. Both engines stopped. Most of the instruments went dark. The nearest big airport was too far away.

The cause was not a leak or a broken engine. It was a number. In a country halfway through switching to the metric system, a fuel calculation mixed up pounds and kilograms, and the jet took off with less than half the fuel it needed.

This is the story of that number, and of the two pilots who turned a 132-tonne airliner into a glider and landed it on an old air force runway in the middle of a car race.
